news.headline: The First 3,000-Pound Pumpkin Ever!
news.body: A grower named Ron Wallace from Rhode Island just set a new world record for the heaviest pumpkin. His giant gourd weighed 3,156 pounds, about as much as a small car! It is the first pumpkin, and the first fruit of any kind, to ever weigh more than 3,000 pounds. Ron planted the seed in his greenhouse in April, and it grew for almost six months. Amazingly, he beat a record that had been set in England just one week earlier, by nearly 300 pounds!

news.headline: A New Pilot Flies NASA's Super-Quiet Speedy Jet
news.body: NASA has a special airplane called the X-59 that can fly faster than the speed of sound. Usually that makes a loud BOOM, but the X-59 is shaped to make only a soft thump instead. This week, NASA test pilot Mike Lippert flew it for the very first time over the California desert. He zoomed to 1.4 times the speed of sound and climbed to 55,000 feet, way higher than regular airliners fly. He said it was a dream come true!

news.headline: A See-Through Snail Is Found in a Dark Cave
news.body: Scientists exploring a cave high in the mountains of China found a brand-new kind of snail. It is tiny, has no eyes at all, and its shell is so clear you can almost see through it! The snail lives in shallow water where sunlight never reaches, so it doesn't need eyes. It is the first freshwater cave snail ever found in China. Scientists named it Erhaia dijiang and hope to learn more about the secret creatures living underground.

fun_fact: Snails have thousands of teeny-tiny teeth on a ribbon-shaped tongue. They use it like a file to scrape up their food! 🐌

did_you_know: A pumpkin is about 90 percent water. That's why giant pumpkins need to drink lots and lots of water to grow so big! 💧
